searchText: We just came across a discrepancy between Geth and Nethermind in our integration tests. When provided a payload for which the parent is unknown, Nethermind returns SYNCING while Geth returns ACCEPTED. It seems that Nethermind is correct in this instance by my reading of the spec More info: https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/pull/3378 I can confirm that EL must return SYNCING in this case, cc <@360491619402776577> ``` // Either no beacon sync was started yet, or it rejected the delivered // payload as non-integratable on top of the existing sync. We'll just // have to rely on the beacon client to forcefully update the head with // a forkchoice update request. ``` This is the only case where we return ACCEPTED instead of SYNCING when we get a new payload with unknown parent. Afaik the spec permits us to not start the sync on newpayload and only force start the sync on fcu ACCEPTED is only allowed when "ancestors of a payload are known and comprise a well-formed chain." Fix: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/25414 Is it important to get it into the goerli release? I don't think it is too important as long as CLs are treating SYNCING/ACCEPTED in exact same way. <@602753420033785856> what's the LH behaviour around these two statuses? Does geth ever responds with ACCEPTED after this fix? Yes, if we don't have the state for the parent block anymore We treat them the same, AFAIK. The only reason we noticed was an equality check in our tests We recently changed the jwt time limit right? Is there any doc for that? https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/authentication.md#jwt-claims And here is the PR: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/256 Thanks! Update on mainnet-shadow-fork-10: - We didn't notice any client incompatibilities with the transition! (🚀) - Some besu nodes were running an older version and needed an update/resync (that'd explain almost all of the missing participation rate). The nodes should be done resyncing soon and the participation rate should go back up. - We noticed lodestar-erigon having trouble fetching a block, but this is most likely attributed to the shadow fork peering setup rather than a real issue. <dannyryan> fantastic work!

excerpts.content:
Update on mainnet-shadow-fork-10:
- We didn't notice any client incompatibilities with the transition! (🚀)
- Some besu nodes were running an older version and needed an update/resync (that'd explain almost all of the missing participation rate). The nodes should be done resyncing soon and the participation rate should go back up.
- We noticed lodestar-erigon having trouble fetching a block, but this is most likely attributed to the shadow fork peering setup rather than a real issue.
